name: Mike Waltz
role: U.S. Representative from Florida (2019–2025), National Security Advisor (2025), U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations (2025–)
summary: Waltz is a Republican former Army Green Beret whose record centres on national security: a China hawk who backs a larger military, NATO and Israel, and wants allies to pay more. He voted against gun-control, abortion-rights and climate bills and for domestic energy production and border-enforcement measures. At the UN he has called for radical transparency and reform while arguing the US should stay at the table.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted for the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act (April 2024), which reauthorized Section 702 foreign-intelligence surveillance with changes.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted no on the Bipartisan Background Checks Act and Enhanced Background Checks Act (2019, 2021) and on the Assault Weapons Ban (2022).

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted yes on the Respect for Marriage Act twice, in July and December 2022, which requires federal recognition of same-sex marriages.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted against passage of the Ensuring Access to Abortion Act (July 2022) and for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (Jan. 2023).

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted no on the Climate Action Now Act (2019) and yes on repealing the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund (2024).

military-superiority.rationale: Told the House he did not want to merely keep pace with China, Russia and others: "We need to have overmatch" to keep the peace and deterrence.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Voted for the 2019 resolution opposing efforts to delegitimize the State of Israel, and for 2023 resolutions standing with Israel.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted yes on the Lower Energy Costs Act, Protecting American Energy Production Act and Restoring American Energy Dominance Act (2023-24), which expand oil and gas production.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Voted for the NATO Support Act (2019) and the 2022 resolution backing Finland and Sweden joining NATO, supporting the permanent alliance.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Voted no on the 2020 bill to remove Confederate statues and busts from the Capitol and no on the 2021 bill to replace statues of Confederate figures.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Voted yes on the POLICE Act (2023) and the Police Our Border Act (2024), which support law enforcement.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voted yes on H.R. 192 (2024, passed 262-143), which prohibits non-citizens from voting in District of Columbia local elections.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Voted for the 2019 resolution affirming the U.S. record on the Armenian Genocide and the 2021 resolution condemning the genocide of Uyghurs.

close-ties-china.rationale: Voted for resolutions condemning Beijing on Tiananmen (2019), Hong Kong (2021) and the Uyghur genocide (2021), and for China sanctions and financial-threat bills.

notes: Themes searched: votes (Voteview, all topics above), House floor speeches and hearings (crec.js by topic: China, NATO, Ukraine, energy, abortion, surveillance, immigration, Second Amendment, union, climate), and the 2025 UN nomination hearing record. Many statements are null because he took no stated position on them. His Jan. 6, 2021 objection votes could not be confirmed (sources conflict) and are not used.
